Kingdom.name: {=taom_erebor_name}Erebor
Kingdom.title: {=taom_erebor_title}Kingdom of Erebor
Kingdom.text: {=taom_erebor_desc}The Lonely Mountain, Erebor, stands as the greatest of the Dwarven kingdoms in the north. Rich in gold and mithril, it is home to the line of Durin. The Dwarves of Erebor are renowned craftsmen and fierce warriors, their halls echoing with the songs of their ancestors.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_rivendell_name}Imladris
Kingdom.title: {=taom_rivendell_title}Refuge of Imladris
Kingdom.text: {=taom_rivendell_desc}Hidden deep within the clefts of the Misty Mountains, Rivendell is the Last Homely House East of the Sea. Founded by Elrond Half-elven, it is a refuge against the gathering dark, a place of healing, lore, and quiet strength.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_mirkwood_name}Lasgalen
Kingdom.title: {=taom_mirkwood_title}Mirkwood Realm
Kingdom.text: {=taom_mirkwood_desc}The Woodland Realm of Mirkwood has endured much hardship over the years. Under the leadership of Thranduil, the Woodelves have become reclusive and wary of strangers. Yet in the heart of Thranduil lingers a fire kindled in the ancient days of the First Age.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_lothlorien_name}Lothlorien
Kingdom.title: {=taom_lothlorien_title}Kingdom of Lóthlorien
Kingdom.text: {=taom_lothlorien_desc}The Golden Wood lies nestled between the Silverlode and the mighty Anduin. Guarded by the will of Galadriel and Celeborn, it stands as a bastion of Elven grace and defiance - a land untouched by time, where the leaves do not fall.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_isengard_name}Isengard
Kingdom.title: {=taom_isengard_title}Overlordship of Isengard
Kingdom.text: {=taom_isengard_desc}Isengard, the stronghold of the White Wizard Saruman, stands as a bastion of power and ambition. The Uruk-hai march forth under the banner of the White Hand, their discipline and savagery unmatched.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_gundabad_name}Gundabad
Kingdom.title: {=taom_gundabad_title}Gundabad
Kingdom.text: {=taom_gundabad_desc}Gundabad, the ancient and foreboding stronghold of the Orcs, stands as a bastion of savagery and domination. The Orcs of Gundabad, bred for war and chaos, rally under bloodied banners.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_umbar_name}Umbar
Kingdom.title: {=taom_umbar_title}Haven of Umbar
Kingdom.text: {=taom_umbar_desc}Umbar, the dark haven of the Corsairs, is a realm steeped in maritime power and treacherous ambition. The Corsairs raid the coasts of Middle-earth, spreading fear with their swift ships.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_dolguldur_name}Dol Guldur
Kingdom.title: {=taom_dolguldur_title}Necromancy of Dol Guldur
Kingdom.text: {=taom_dolguldur_desc}Dol Guldur, the fortress of shadow and despair, stands as a menacing beacon of the Necromancer's dark will. The Orcs and foul creatures that inhabit its depths strike fear into the hearts of all.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_shaghana_name}Shaghâna
Kingdom.title: {=taom_shaghana_title}Taskralan of Shaghâna
Kingdom.text: {=taom_shaghana_desc}Shaghâna is the eastern reach of Harad, a land of sun-scorched steppes and ancient fortresses. Its nine tribal clans are fierce warriors, bound together by oath and blood, striking fear into those who dare oppose them.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_abanissa_name}Âbanissa
Kingdom.title: {=taom_abanissa_title}Châjaphân of Âbanissa
Kingdom.text: {=taom_abanissa_desc}Âbanissa lies in the deep south of Harad, a realm of humid jungles and ancient stone dynasties. The great Houses of Âbanissa command fearsome war-beasts and armies of disciplined warriors, their power answerable to none but Sauron himself.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_goblin_name}Goblins
Kingdom.title: {=taom_goblin_title}Goblin-Realm of the High Pass
Kingdom.text: {=taom_goblin_desc}The Goblins of the High Pass swarm the tunnels beneath the Misty Mountains, the spawn of the host the Great Goblin once led against dwarf and wayfarer alike. Numberless and vicious, they pour from Goblin-town to raid the mountain roads.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_mistymountainorcs_name}Misty Mountain Orcs
Kingdom.title: {=taom_mistymountainorcs_title}Orc-Host of the Misty Mountains
Kingdom.text: {=taom_mistymountainorcs_desc}The orc-host of the Misty Mountains holds the high places and deep delvings from Mount Gram to the gates of Moria. Bred for war in the cold peaks, they answer the call of the Shadow and hunger to reclaim the mountains for their own.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_bluecraig_name}Goblins of Blue Craig
Kingdom.title: {=taom_bluecraig_title}Goblin-Realm of Blue Craig
Kingdom.text: {=taom_bluecraig_desc}The goblin-warrens of Blue Craig in the Blue Mountains (Ered Luin) of the far west, hard by the Grey Havens of Lindon. A distinct, numberless host of goblin-kind — separate from their Misty Mountains cousins of Goblin Town — they swarm the western crags and trouble the Elves of the western shore.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_lindon_name}Lindon
Kingdom.title: {=taom_lindon_title}High Kingdom of Lindon
Kingdom.text: {=taom_lindon_desc}Lindon, the green land west of the Blue Mountains, is the last realm of the High Elves upon the shores of Middle-earth. From the Grey Havens of Mithlond the white ships sail into the West, while Círdan the Shipwright keeps watch over the fading light of the Eldar.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_arthedain_name}Arthedain
Kingdom.title: {=taom_arthedain_title}North-Kingdom of Arthedain
Kingdom.text: {=taom_arthedain_desc}The last of the three realms into which Arnor was sundered, Arthedain did not fall. Arvedui's line still holds Fornost upon the North Downs, though its lords are few, its towns poor, and Angmar's shadow lies always on the northern hills.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_cardolan_name}Cardolan
Kingdom.title: {=taom_cardolan_title}Kingdom of Cardolan
Kingdom.text: {=taom_cardolan_desc}The southern of the three realms into which Arnor was sundered. Its kings lie in the barrows of Tyrn Gorthad and its riders keep the plains between the Baranduin and the Greyflood, but its towns are few and its lords contend with Arthedain and Rhudaur for the crown of Arnor.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_rhudaur_name}Rhudaur
Kingdom.title: {=taom_rhudaur_title}Kingdom of Rhudaur
Kingdom.text: {=taom_rhudaur_desc}The eastern of the three realms into which Arnor was sundered, a hill kingdom between the Hoarwell and the Loudwater. Its Dunedain lords hold Cameth Brin and the Angle and rule a hard people of hill-men, with trolls in the fells and orcs on every pass.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_eredluin_name}Ered Luin
Kingdom.title: {=taom_eredluin_title}Kingdom of Ered Luin
Kingdom.text: {=taom_eredluin_desc}The dwarf kingdom of the Blue Mountains. Durin's Folk made Thorin's Halls there in their exile, and in this age the Broadbeams and the Firebeards hold Belegost and Nogrod again. Its lords are few and its halls are poorer than those of its kin in the east, but its smiths are the oldest in the West, and its axes keep the goblins of Blue Craig from the roads to Lindon.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_anduinvale_name}Anduin Vale
Kingdom.title: {=taom_anduinvale_title}Anduin Vale
Kingdom.text: {=taom_anduinvale_desc}The Beornings and the Woodmen of the Vales hold the upper Anduin between the Misty Mountains and Mirkwood. They keep the High Pass and the Old Ford open for honest travellers and take a heavy toll of orcs and wolves. Their chieftains hold Beorn's Hall and the Carrock and want no part in the wars of kings.

Kingdom.name: {=taom_angaladh_name}Angáladh
Kingdom.title: {=taom_angaladh_title}Kingdom of Angáladh
Kingdom.text: {=taom_angaladh_desc}The Woodmen of western Mirkwood cleared their steads under the eaves of the forest and named their realm for the iron-hard trees that ring Woodmen-town. They are bowmen and woodwards, few in number, at peace with the Elves to the north and ever watchful of Dol Guldur to the south.
